In this case, we have an indeterminate form of type $\frac{\infty }{\infty },$ so applying  L'Hopital's rule yields

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{e}^{x}} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{[x\operatorname{ln}⁡x]^{′}}{[{e}^{x}]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{{e}^{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{\infty }{\infty }.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{e}^{x}} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1}{{e}^{x}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{[\operatorname{ln}⁡x+1]^{′}}{[{e}^{x}]^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{x})}{{e}^{x}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1}{x{e}^{x}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
